The professional count is held flat at 2.0 million from 2022 to 2025 while the total grows by 16.6 million, so every net entrant is an amateur by construction; the definition of professional slides from earning over $100,000 to self-description; and the companion statistic in wide circulation, that 3% of YouTubers take 90% of the wealth, is a unit transformation of a peer-reviewed finding that on average 85% of *views* accrue to 3% of channels [[opus-4-youtube-channels-uploads-and-views-a-statistical-analysis-of-the-past-10]].

The companion 8-million Indonesian creator headcount appears nowhere in the primary report and nowhere in the vendor's own methodology summary [[the-tiktok-effect]] [[tiktoks-socio-economic-impact-in-southeast-asia-a-summary-of-the-report-kadence]].

The companion 8-million Indonesian creator headcount appears nowhere in the primary report and nowhere in the vendor's own methodology summary [[the-tiktok-effect]] [[tiktoks-socio-economic-impact-in-southeast-asia-a-summary-of-the-report-kadence]].

The failure is the merger: two figures from different sources, years and methods were welded into one statistic at a parliamentary hearing — where the same official, pressed for Indonesia revenue, stated on record that he did not have the data [[anggota-dpr-cecar-omzet-tiktok-mengaku-belum-siap-data-teknologi]] — and then repeated as a national statistic.

One further figure cannot be converted into a per-creator quantity at all: a widely circulated channel-count composite is described by its own author as manual open-source intelligence assembled from third-party analytics vendors, because YouTube publishes neither figure [[how-many-youtube-channels-are-there-in-2026-tim-queen]].

A YouTube channel census built from 1.21 billion Internet Archive captures, covering at least 106 million unique channels with subscriber histories back to 2006, is public and has not yet carried a survival model — though its coverage bias correlates with subscriber count and would undercount small-channel deaths, where attrition is highest [[tube-census]].

Indonesia's 2026 Economic Census is billed as the first national instrument to enumerate content-creator business actors [[bps-dan-kemenekraf-bersinergi-kreator-lokal-dilibatkan-dalam-sosialisasi-se2026]], and the standard due at the 22nd International Conference of Labour Statisticians in 2028 would make national platform-work counts comparable for the first time [[ilo-brief]].
